stages.title: PBN Introduction · Navigation Specifications

sections.heading: Introduction to PBN
paragraphs: PBN은 Area Navigation(RNAV)의 큰 틀 아래에서 운용된다. 절차 제목에서 RNAV라는 말은 항공기 장비 수준과 무관하게 “area navigation”을 뜻한다.
PBN에는 두 가지 주요 navigation specification 계열이 있다: RNAV와 RNP. RNAV x의 숫자는 해당 NavSpec의 lateral navigation accuracy 값을 뜻한다.
PBN 요구를 충족하려면 지정된 RNAV 또는 RNP accuracy를 비행시간의 최소 95% 동안 달성해야 한다.
RNP는 RNAV에 onboard performance monitoring and alerting capability를 추가한 개념이다. Jeppesen은 RAIM을 그 예로 든다.

NavSpec은 특정 airspace concept 안에서 navigation application을 지원하기 위해 필요한 aircraft 및 aircrew requirements의 집합이다. RNAV와 RNP 모두 숫자는 NM 단위 lateral accuracy를 나타내며, 해당 공역·route·procedure에서 운항하는 항공기 population이 비행시간의 최소 95% 동안 달성할 것으로 기대되는 값이다.
세부 기준은 ICAO Doc 9613 PBN Manual과 FAA AC 90-105의 관련 내용을 참고하도록 원문이 안내한다.

paragraphs: 이 블록은 이번 Section 2 패치에서 임의 요약으로 빠지는 내용을 막기 위해 해당 페이지의 원문 텍스트 레이어를 그대로 보존한 검수용 원문이다.
GENERAL
a. Introduction to PBN. As air travel has evolved, methods of navigation have improved to
give operators more flexibility. PBN exists under the umbrella of area navigation (RNAV).
The term RNAV in this context, as in procedure titles, just means “area navigation,” regard-
less of the equipment capability of the aircraft. (See FIG 1-2-1.) Many operators have upgra-
ded their systems to obtain the benefits of PBN. Within PBN there are two main categories of
navigation methods or specifications: area navigation (RNAV) and required navigation per-
formance (RNP). In this context, the term RNAV x means a specific navigation specification
with a specified lateral accuracy value. For an aircraft to meet the requirements of PBN, a
specified RNAV or RNP accuracy must be met 95 percent of the flight time. RNP is a PBN
system that includes onboard performance monitoring and alerting capability (for example,
Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring (RAIM)). PBN also introduces the concept of navi-
gation specifications (NavSpecs) which are a set of aircraft and aircrew requirements
needed to support a navigation application within a defined airspace concept. For both RNP
and RNAV NavSpecs, the numerical designation refers to the lateral navigation accuracy in
nautical miles which is expected to be achieved at least 95 percent of the flight time by the
population of aircraft operating within the airspace, route, or procedure. This information is
detailed in International Civil Aviation Organization’s (ICAO) Doc 9613, Performance-based
Navigation (PBN) Manual and the latest FAA AC 90-105, Approval Guidance for RNP Oper-
ations and Barometric Vertical Navigation in the U.S. National Airspace System and in
Remote and Oceanic Airspace.

stages.title: RNAV General · Waypoints

sections.heading: Area Navigation (RNAV) — General
paragraphs: RNAV는 ground- 또는 space-based navigation aids의 coverage 안, self-contained aids의 capability 한계 안, 또는 이들의 조합을 이용하여 원하는 flight path로 운항할 수 있게 하는 navigation method이다.
Jeppesen은 향후 ground-based NAVAID로 정의되는 route보다 RNAV 의존도가 커질 것으로 설명하며, RNAV route와 terminal procedures(DP, STAR 포함)는 RNAV systems를 염두에 두고 설계된다고 설명한다.
RNAV의 잠재적 장점으로 time/fuel savings, radar vector·altitude·speed assignment 의존도 감소에 따른 ATC radio transmission 감소, 더 효율적인 airspace use를 제시한다.
미국 domestic RNAV DP/STAR/route guidance는 AC 90-100도 참고하도록 안내한다.

sections.heading: RNAV Operations
paragraphs: DP/STAR 같은 RNAV procedure는 procedure centerline에 대한 엄격한 awareness와 유지가 필요하다.
조종사는 aircraft navigation system의 working knowledge를 갖고 절차를 적절하게 비행해야 하며, RNAV procedure에서 쓰이는 waypoint type과 leg type을 이해해야 한다.

sections.heading: Waypoints
paragraphs: Waypoint는 latitude/longitude coordinate로 정의되는 predetermined geographical position이며, 단순 named point일 수도 있고 기존 NAVAID·intersection·fix와 연계될 수도 있다.
Waypoint는 desired path에서 direction, speed, altitude change를 나타내는 데 자주 쓰인다.
Fly-by waypoint에서는 두 route segment를 나누는 waypoint에 도달하기 전에 다음 course로의 turn을 시작한다. 이를 turn anticipation이라 한다.
Fly-over waypoint에서는 turn을 시작하기 전에 반드시 waypoint 위를 통과해야 한다.

b. Area Navigation (RNAV)
1. General. RNAV is a method of navigation that permits aircraft operation on any desired
flight path within the coverage of ground- or space-based navigation aids or within the
limits of the capability of self-contained aids, or a combination of these. In the future,
there will be an increased dependence on the use of RNAV in lieu of routes defined by
ground-based navigation aids. RNAV routes and terminal procedures, including depar-
ture procedures (DPs) and standard terminal arrivals (STARs), are designed with RNAV
systems in mind. There are several potential advantages of RNAV routes and proce-
dures:
(a) Time and fuel savings;
(b) Reduced dependence on radar vectoring, altitude, and speed assignments allow-
ing a reduction in required ATC radio transmissions; and
(c) More efficient use of airspace.
In addition to information found in this manual, guidance for domestic RNAV DPs,
STARs, and routes may also be found in AC 90-100, U.S. Terminal and En Route Area
Navigation (RNAV) Operations.
2. RNAV Operations. RNAV procedures, such as DPs and STARs, demand strict pilot
awareness and maintenance of the procedure centerline. Pilots should possess a work-
ing knowledge of their aircraft navigation system to ensure RNAV procedures are flown
in an appropriate manner. In addition, pilots should have an understanding of the vari-
ous waypoint and leg types used in RNAV procedures; these are discussed in more
detail below.
(a) Waypoints. A waypoint is a predetermined geographical position that is defined in
terms of latitude/longitude coordinates. Waypoints may be a simple named point in
space or associated with existing navaids, intersections, or fixes. A waypoint is
most often used to indicate a change in direction, speed, or altitude along the
desired path. RNAV procedures make use of both fly-over and fly-by waypoints.
(1) Fly-by waypoints. Fly-by waypoints are used when an aircraft should begin a
turn to the next course prior to reaching the waypoint separating the two route
segments. This is known as turn anticipation.
(2) Fly-over waypoints. Fly-over waypoints are used when the aircraft must fly
over the point prior to starting a turn.
NOTE: FIG 1-2-2 illustrates several differences between a fly-by and a fly-
over waypoint.

stages.title: RNAV Leg Types · TF/DF/CF/RF/Heading

sections.heading: Path and Terminator Concept
paragraphs: RNAV leg type은 waypoint 이전·이후·사이의 desired path를 설명한다. 두 글자 code는 path(heading/course/track 등)와 termination point(altitude/distance/fix 등)를 나타낸다.
Procedure design에 사용되는 leg type은 aircraft navigation database에 포함되지만 보통 procedure chart에는 직접 표시되지 않는다. Chart의 narrative depiction이 절차를 어떻게 비행하는지 설명한다.
Path and terminator concept의 핵심은 모든 leg가 termination point를 가지며 그 termination point로 들어가는 어떤 형태의 path를 가진다는 것이다.

sections.heading: Track to Fix (TF)
paragraphs: TF leg는 다음 waypoint까지의 flight track을 intercept하고 acquire하는 경로이며 point-to-point leg라고도 불린다. 원문 narrative 예시는 “direct ALPHA, then on course to BRAVO WP.”이다.

figure.caption: FIG 1-2-3 · Track to Fix Leg Type · p.396

sections.heading: Direct to Fix (DF)
paragraphs: DF leg는 initial area에서 다음 waypoint로 직접 향하는 aircraft track으로 정의된다. 원문 narrative 예시는 “turn right direct BRAVO WP.”이다.

figure.caption: FIG 1-2-4 · Direct to Fix Leg Type · p.396

sections.heading: Course to Fix (CF)
paragraphs: CF leg는 지정된 course를 가지고 fix에서 끝나는 path이다. 원문 narrative 예시는 “on course 150 to ALPHA WP.”이다.

figure.caption: FIG 1-2-5 · Course to Fix Leg Type · p.397

sections.heading: Radius to Fix (RF)
paragraphs: RF leg는 defined turn center 주위의 constant-radius circular path이며 fix에서 종료된다.

figure.caption: FIG 1-2-6 · Radius to Fix Leg Type · p.397

sections.heading: Heading Legs
paragraphs: Heading leg의 예로 Heading to Altitude(VA), Heading to DME range(VD), Heading to Manual Termination/Vector(VM)이 있다. 원문은 “climb heading 350 to 1500”, “heading 265, at 9 DME west of PXR VORTAC, right turn heading 360”, “fly heading 090, expect radar vectors to DRYHT INT.”를 narrative 예로 든다.

(b) RNAV Leg Types. A leg type describes the desired path proceeding, following, or
between waypoints on an RNAV procedure. Leg types are identified by a two-letter
code that describes the path (e.g., heading, course, track, etc.) and the termination
point (e.g., the path terminates at an altitude, distance, fix, etc.). Leg types used for
procedure design are included in the aircraft navigation database, but not normally
provided on the procedure chart. The narrative depiction of the RNAV chart
describes how a procedure is flown. The “path and terminator concept” defines
that every leg of a procedure has a termination point and some kind of path into
that termination point. Some of the available leg types are described below.
(1) Track to Fix. A Track to Fix (TF) leg is intercepted and acquired as the flight
track to the following waypoint. Track to a Fix legs are sometimes called
point-to-point legs for this reason. Narrative: “direct ALPHA, then on course
to BRAVO WP.” See FIG 1-2-3.
(2) Direct to Fix. A Direct to Fix (DF) leg is a path described by an aircraft’s track
from an initial area direct to the next waypoint. Narrative: “turn right direct
BRAVO WP.” See FIG 1-2-4.

stages.title: Navigation Issues · FMS

sections.heading: Navigation Issues
paragraphs: 조종사는 navigation system inputs, alerts, annunciations를 이해해야 하며 particular sensor/system의 availability와 suitability를 고려해야 한다.
GPS/WAAS: TSO-C129(), C196(), C145(), C146() systems 사용자는 departure와 arrival airports를 입력하여 proper RAIM availability와 CDI sensitivity를 확보해야 한다.
DME/DME: position updating은 navigation system logic뿐 아니라 DME facility proximity, availability, geometry, signal masking에 의존한다.
VOR/DME: VOR의 고유 특성 때문에 GPS 또는 DME/DME position updating보다 less accurate한 값이 나올 수 있다.
Inertial Navigation: IRU/INS는 DME/DME 또는 GPS와 결합되어 overall navigation performance를 개선하는 경우가 많다. Specific inertial position updating requirements가 적용될 수 있다는 NOTE가 있다.

sections.heading: Flight Management System (FMS)
paragraphs: FMS는 sensors, receivers, computers와 navigation database가 통합된 suite이며 displays 및 automatic flight control systems에 performance와 RNAV guidance를 제공한다.
GPS, DME, VOR, LOC, IRU 등 여러 source를 입력으로 받을 수 있고 한 번에 하나 또는 조합으로 navigation solution에 적용할 수 있다. 일부 FMS는 faulty navigation information의 detection/isolation 기능을 제공한다.
Appropriate signal이 있을 때 FMS는 보통 GPS 및/또는 DME/DME를 position update에 주로 사용하며 architecture와 source geometry에 따라 다른 input도 통합될 수 있다.
DME/DME와 하나 이상의 IRU를 결합한 입력은 DME/DME/IRU 또는 D/D/I로 약칭하는 경우가 많다.

(c) Navigation Issues. Pilots should be aware of their navigation system inputs,
alerts, and annunciations in order to make better-informed decisions. In addition,
the availability and suitability of particular sensors/systems should be considered.
(1) GPS/WAAS. Operators using TSO-C129(), TSO-C196(), TSO-C145() or
TSO-C146() systems should ensure departure and arrival airports are entered
to ensure proper RAIM availability and CDI sensitivity.
(2) DME/DME. Operators should be aware that DME/DME position updating is
dependent on navigation system logic and DME facility proximity, availability,
geometry, and signal masking.
(3) VOR/DME. Unique VOR characteristics may result in less accurate values
from VOR/DME position updating than from GPS or DME/DME position
updating.
(4) Inertial Navigation. Inertial reference units and inertial navigation systems
are often coupled with other types of navigation inputs, e.g., DME/DME or
GPS, to improve overall navigation system performance.
NOTE: Specific inertial position updating requirements may apply.
(d) Flight Management System (FMS). An FMS is an integrated suite of sensors,
receivers, and computers, coupled with a navigation database. These systems
generally provide performance and RNAV guidance to displays and automatic
flight control systems.
Inputs can be accepted from multiple sources such as GPS, DME, VOR, LOC and
IRU. These inputs may be applied to a navigation solution one at a time or in com-
bination. Some FMSs provide for the detection and isolation of faulty navigation
information.
When appropriate navigation signals are available, FMSs will normally rely on GPS
and/or DME/DME (that is, the use of distance information from two or more DME
stations) for position updates. Other inputs may also be incorporated based on
FMS system architecture and navigation source geometry.
NOTE: DME/DME inputs coupled with one or more IRU(s) are often abbreviated
as DME/DME/IRU or D/D/I.
(e) RNAV Navigation Specifications (Nav Specs)
Nav Specs are a set of aircraft and aircrew requirements needed to support a navi-
gation application within a defined airspace concept. For both RNP and RNAV
designations, the numerical designation refers to the lateral navigation accuracy in
nautical miles which is expected to be achieved at least 95 percent of the flight
time by the population of aircraft operating within the airspace, route, or procedure.
(See FIG 1-2-1.)

stages.title: RNAV NavSpecs · RNP General

sections.heading: RNAV Navigation Specifications
paragraphs: NavSpec은 defined airspace concept에서 navigation application을 지원하기 위한 aircraft/aircrew requirements의 집합이다. RNP와 RNAV 숫자는 NM 단위 lateral accuracy를 나타내며 비행시간의 최소 95% 동안 달성되어야 한다.
RNAV 1은 보통 DP와 STAR에 사용되며 total system error가 비행시간의 95% 동안 1 NM를 넘지 않아야 한다.
RNAV 2는 별도 지정이 없으면 보통 en route operations에 사용된다. T-route와 Q-route가 예이며 total system error가 비행시간의 95% 동안 2 NM를 넘지 않아야 한다.
RNAV 10은 보통 oceanic operations에 사용된다. 원문은 RNP 10과 RNAV 10 terminology 관계의 자세한 내용은 paragraph 4-7-1을 보라고 안내한다.

sections.heading: Required Navigation Performance (RNP) — General
paragraphs: RNAV NavSpec과 RNP NavSpec 모두 performance requirements를 갖지만 RNP는 onboard performance monitoring and alerting(OBPMA)을 추가로 요구한다.
RNP는 defined airspace에서 운항하기 위해 필요한 navigation performance의 statement이기도 하다. Aircraft navigation system이 실제 성능을 monitor하고 operational requirement 충족 여부를 pilot에게 알리는 능력이 핵심이다.
OBPMA는 ATC intervention 및/또는 procedural separation에 대한 의존을 줄이는 데 기여한다. Aircraft RNP capability는 overall containment를 위한 separation criteria 결정의 주요 요소이다.
RNP capability는 aircraft equipment와 navigation infrastructure에 따라 달라질 수 있다. Aircraft가 RNP 1 eligible이어도 NAVAID coverage 제한 또는 avionics failure로 실제 RNP 1 operation을 못 할 수 있다.
AFM 또는 avionics documents에는 aircraft의 RNP eligibilities가 명확히 기재되어야 하며, 누락·불완전하면 manufacturer에 확인하도록 원문이 권고한다.
NavSpec은 lateral accuracy 숫자가 더 작다고 무조건 “better”인 것이 아니라 서로 다른 specification이다. RNP 1 eligibility가 RNP 2 또는 RNAV 1 eligibility를 자동 의미하지 않는다.
FAA safeguard로 aircraft navigation database는 aircraft가 eligibility를 유지하는 procedures만 보유하도록 요구된다. 특정 procedure가 database에 없다면 aircraft가 그 PBN element에 ineligible이거나 계산/비행할 수 없는 가능성이 있다.
RF turns 또는 scalability 같은 optional capability는 AFM/avionics documents에 기술되어야 하며, database에서 procedure를 load한 후 avionics capability를 사용해 waypoint/track data를 확인해야 한다.

(1) RNAV 1. Typically RNAV 1 is used for DPs and STARs and appears on the
charts. Aircraft must maintain a total system error of not more than 1 NM for
95 percent of the total flight time.
(2) RNAV 2. Typically RNAV 2 is used for en route operations unless otherwise
specified. T-routes and Q-routes are examples of this Nav Spec. Aircraft must
maintain a total system error of not more than 2 NM for 95 percent of the total
flight time.
(3) RNAV 10. Typically RNAV 10 is used in oceanic operations. See paragraph
4-7-1 for specifics and explanation of the relationship between RNP 10 and
RNAV 10 terminology.
REQUIRED NAVIGATION PERFORMANCE (RNP)
a. General. While both RNAV navigation specifications (NavSpecs) and RNP NavSpecs con-
tain specific performance requirements, RNP is RNAV with the added requirement for
onboard performance monitoring and alerting (OBPMA). RNP is also a statement of naviga-
tion performance necessary for operation within a defined airspace. A critical component of
RNP is the ability of the aircraft navigation system to monitor its achieved navigation per-
formance, and to identify for the pilot whether the operational requirement is, or is not, being
met during an operation. OBPMA capability therefore allows a lessened reliance on air traffic
control intervention and/or procedural separation to achieve the overall safety of the opera-
tion. RNP capability of the aircraft is a major component in determining the separation crite-
ria to ensure that the overall containment of the operation is met. The RNP capability of an
aircraft will vary depending upon the aircraft equipment and the navigation infrastructure. For
example, an aircraft may be eligible for RNP 1, but may not be capable of RNP 1 operations
due to limited NAVAID coverage or avionics failure. The Aircraft Flight Manual (AFM) or
avionics documents for your aircraft should specifically state the aircraft’s RNP eligibilities.
Contact the manufacturer of the avionics or the aircraft if this information is missing or incom-
plete. NavSpecs should be considered different from one another, not “better” or “worse”
based on the described lateral navigation accuracy. It is this concept that requires each Nav-
Spec eligbility to be listed separately in the avionics documents or AFM. For example, RNP 1
is different from RNAV 1, and an RNP 1 eligibility does NOT mean automatic RNP 2 or
RNAV 1 eligibility. As a safeguard, the FAA requires that aircraft navigation databases hold
only those procedures that the aircraft maintains eligibility for. If you look for a specific instru-
ment procedure in your aircraft’s navigation database and cannot find it, it’s likely that proce-
dure contains PBN elements your aircraft is ineligible for or cannot compute and fly. Further,
optional capabilities such as Radius-to-fix (RF) turns or scalability should be described in the
AFM or avionics documents. Use the capabilities of your avionics suite to verify the appropri-
ate waypoint and track data after loading the procedure from your database.
b. PBN Operations.
1. Lateral Accuracy Values. Lateral Accuracy values are applicable to a selected air-
space, route, or procedure. The lateral accuracy value is a value typically expressed as
a distance in nautical miles from the intended centerline of a procedure, route, or path.

sections.heading: Lateral Accuracy Values
paragraphs: Lateral accuracy value는 selected airspace, route, procedure에 적용되며 intended centerline에서의 NM 거리로 표현된다. RNP application은 예를 들어 RNP lateral accuracy의 2배 같은 multiple에서의 potential error도 고려한다.

sections.heading: RNP Approach (RNP APCH)
paragraphs: 미국에서 RNP APCH는 chart title이 RNAV (GPS)이며 LNAV, LNAV/VNAV, LPV, LP 등 여러 minima line을 제공한다.
GPS는 SBAS 유무와 관계없이 LNAV minima의 lateral information을 제공할 수 있다. LNAV/VNAV는 LNAV lateral에 barometric VNAV 또는 SBAS vertical guidance를 결합한다.
LPV 또는 LP minima를 사용하려면 SBAS를 사용해야 한다.
RF turn capability는 RNP APCH eligibility에서 optional이다. RNP APCH eligible이어도 avionics feature에 RF turn이 명시되지 않으면 RF turn을 비행할 수 없다.
GLS procedure도 RNP APCH NavSpec을 사용해 구성되며 precision approach capability를 제공한다.
RNP APCH lateral accuracy는 terminal 및 missed approach segment에서 1이며 final approach에서는 본질적으로 RNP 0.3까지 scale한다(SBAS 사용 시 40 m).

sections.heading: RNP Authorization Required Approach (RNP AR APCH)
paragraphs: 미국에서 RNP AR APCH의 chart title은 RNAV (RNP)이다.
엄격한 equipage/pilot training standards와 special FAA authorization이 필요하다. Scalability와 RF turn capability는 mandatory이다.
Vertical navigation performance는 barometric VNAV 또는 SBAS를 기반으로 한다.

RNP AR은 특정 location에서 specific benefit을 제공하기 위한 것으로 모든 operator/aircraft를 위한 것이 아니다. Required target level of safety를 위해 specific aircraft performance, design, operational processes, training, procedure design criteria가 필요하다.
Terminal/missed approach에서 lateral accuracy가 1 아래로 내려갈 수 있고 final approach에서는 RNP 0.3 이하까지 scale할 수 있다. 원문은 AC 90-101과 paragraph 5-4-18을 참고하도록 안내한다.

sections.heading: RNP Authorization Required Departure (RNP AR DP)
paragraphs: RNP AR DP는 RNP AR approach와 유사하게 stringent equipage/pilot training standards 및 special FAA authorization이 필요하다.
Scalability와 RF turn capability는 RNP AR DP eligibility에서 mandatory이다.

특정 location의 specific benefit을 위한 것으로 모든 operator/aircraft를 대상으로 하지 않는다. Required target level of safety를 위해 specific performance, design, operational processes, training, procedure design criteria가 필요하다.
Initial departure flight path에서 lateral accuracy는 RNP 0.3보다 낮게 scale하지 않는다. 원문은 AC 90-101 및 paragraph 5-4-18을 참고하도록 한다.

sections.heading: Advanced RNP (A-RNP)
paragraphs: A-RNP는 aircraft avionics suite에 minimum mandatory functions가 enable된 NavSpec이다. 미국의 minimum functions에는 RF turns 계산/수행, scalable RNP, parallel offset flight path generation이 포함된다.
일부 oceanic/remote continental airspace에서는 dual systems 같은 higher continuity가 요구될 수 있다. Fixed radius transitions와 Time of Arrival Control 같은 일부 en route advanced option은 미국에서는 optional이다.
보통 A-RNP eligible aircraft는 RNP APCH, RNP/RNAV 1, RNP/RNAV 2, RNP 4, RNP/RNAV 10 운항에도 eligible하다.
Terminal environment에서 1.0 또는 0.3의 scalable RNP lateral value를 허용한다. Reduced lateral accuracy 사용은 보통 autopilot 및/또는 flight director 사용을 요구한다.
A-RNP eligible aircraft가 RNP AR APCH 또는 RNP AR DP에 자동 eligible한 것은 아니다. RNP AR은 별도의 eligibility determination과 special FAA authorization이 필요하다.

sections.heading: RNP 1 / 2 / 4 / 10 / 0.3
paragraphs: RNP 1은 terminal arrival/departure와 PBN segment가 포함된 conventional procedure의 initial/intermediate approach phase에 lateral accuracy 1을 요구한다. RF turn은 optional이다.
RNP 2는 domestic와 oceanic/remote operations에 lateral accuracy 2로 적용된다.
RNP 4는 oceanic/remote operations에만 lateral accuracy 4로 적용되며 RNP 4 eligibility는 자동으로 RNP 10 eligibility를 부여한다.

RNP 10 NavSpec은 일부 oceanic/remote operation에 lateral accuracy 10으로 적용된다. 그 airspace에서는 RNAV 10 NavSpec이 적용되므로 RNP 10 eligible aircraft는 RNAV 10 operation eligible로 간주된다. RNP 4 eligible aircraft도 자동으로 RNP 10/RNAV 10에 qualified된다.

RNP 0.3 NavSpec은 authorized flight phases에서 lateral accuracy 0.3을 요구하지만 oceanic, remote, final approach segment에는 authorized되지 않는다. 원문은 처음에는 rotorcraft operation에 적용되며 slow-flying fixed-wing application은 검토 중이라고 설명한다. RF turn은 optional이다.
Charted RNP value 0.30과 NavSpec title “RNP 0.3”을 혼동하지 말아야 한다. Charted RNP 0.30 이하 값은 RNP 0.15/0.10/0.30처럼 두 decimal place로 표시될 수 있지만 NavSpec title은 RNP 0.3이라고만 한다.

sections.heading: Application / Depiction of PBN Requirements
paragraphs: U.S. standard lateral accuracy values는 특정 navigation sensor(GPS 등) 또는 적절한 performance의 multi-sensor RNAV systems에 기초할 수 있다.
미국에서 procedure에 적용되는 PBN requirements는 chart/procedure에 별도의 standardized PBN notes box로 prominently 표시된다.

PBN box에는 해당 NavSpec(s)와 필요 시 required sensor/infrastructure, additional/advanced functional requirements, minimum RNP value, amplifying remarks가 포함된다. 이 box의 항목은 procedure의 PBN element를 비행하기 위한 REQUIRED 사항이다.
예를 들어 RNAV missed approach가 있는 ILS는 missed approach에 필요한 capability를 PBN box에 명시한다.
별도의 Equipment Requirements box는 ground-based equipment 및/또는 airport-specific requirements를 표시한다. PBN element와 ground-based equipment requirement가 모두 있으면 PBN requirements box가 먼저 나온다.

Out-of-service NAVAID 대신 RNAV를 substitute means로 쓰려는 경우 pilot이 ATC에 intent/capability를 알려야 할 수 있다.

stages.title: GPS Jamming / Spoofing

sections.heading: Vulnerability and Sources
paragraphs: GPS satellite의 low-strength data transmission signal은 navigation reliability를 크게 낮출 수 있는 anomaly에 취약하다. GPS는 communication, navigation, surveillance, safety systems, automation 등 여러 aviation function에 쓰이므로 pilot은 equipment performance anomaly를 면밀히 monitor하고 apparent GPS degradation을 ATC에 promptly inform해야 하며 GPS 없이 운항할 준비도 해야 한다.

Unintentional interference source로 radar, microwave links, ionosphere effects, solar activity, multi-path error, satellite communications, GPS repeaters, 일부 onboard systems가 열거된다. 이런 interference는 일반적으로 localized/intermittent하다.
더 큰 concern은 jammer/spoofer를 이용한 intentional unauthorized interference이다.
U.S. government의 GPS tests/training/exercises도 GPS signal을 방해할 수 있지만 geographically limited, coordinated, scheduled되고 GPS/WAAS NOTAM으로 공지된다. GPS aircraft operator는 route의 GPS/WAAS NOTAM을 항상 확인해야 한다.

sections.heading: Possible Impacts
paragraphs: GPS navigation 사용 불가, hybrid GPS-inertial navigation 사용 불가, PBN capability loss/degradation(RNP procedure 비행 불가 등)이 발생할 수 있다.
TAWS triggering이 unreliable해질 수 있고 navigation display/moving map/EFB의 aircraft position이 부정확할 수 있다.
ADS-B output이 loss 또는 erroneous가 될 수 있다.
Spoofing으로 intended path에서 벗어나면 autotuning이 nearby NAVAID를 선택하지 않는 등 conventional NAVAID 사용에도 unexpected effect가 생길 수 있다.
Erroneous insufficient-fuel indication 같은 position-dependent FMS effect가 생길 수 있다.
GPS 의존 ATM infrastructure와 관련 system failure/degradation으로 airspace infringement 또는 route deviation이 생길 수 있다.
Aircraft clock failure/오류로 CPDLC logon이 불가능해질 수 있고, wind/ground speed indication도 잘못될 수 있다.

sections.heading: IFR Cross-check and Pre-departure
paragraphs: IFR 비행에서는 intended route에 대한 additional navigation equipment를 갖추고 VOR/DME 등으로 routine position cross-check를 해 compromised GPS signal을 탐지할 수 있도록 해야 한다.
GPS anomaly 때문에 VOR navigation으로 전환할 때는 Chart Supplement U.S.에서 VOR MON과 연계된 conventional approach available airport를 확인하도록 원문이 안내한다.
출발 전 FAA 권고: potential risk location 인지, relevant NOTAM 확인, fuel contingency 계획, destination에서 conventional NAVAID 및 적절한 arrival/approach 사용 계획, 해당 OEM의 detailed guidance 준수.

sections.heading: During Flight
paragraphs: Aircraft type/avionics별 manufacturer guidance를 확인하고 GPS disruption indication에 vigilant해야 하며 가능하면 conventional NAVAID로 aircraft position을 verify한다.

Jamming/spoofing indication 예: actual navigation performance 변화, aircraft clock 오류, incorrect FMS position, displayed GPS position의 큰 shift, PFD/ND position-error warning, 다른 aircraft의 clock/position error 보고 또는 vector 요청.
GPS capability loss로 발생하는 operational risk/limitation 및 GPS signal input을 요구하는 onboard systems 영향을 평가한다.
Intended route/approach에 critical한 NAVAID availability를 확인하고 conventional IFR procedure로 revert할 준비를 유지한다.
GPS anomaly를 경험하면 ATC에 promptly notify한다. 다만 이미 NOTAM으로 공지된 known testing area를 통과 중이고 ATC assistance가 필요하지 않으면 jamming/spoofing을 ATC에 보고하지 않아도 된다고 원문이 설명한다.

sections.heading: Post-flight
paragraphs: GPS jamming/spoofing은 maintenance log에 기록하여 모든 fault가 cleared되도록 하고, FAA의 “Report a GPS Anomaly” reporting site에 detailed report를 제출하도록 권고한다.

RECOGNIZING, MITIGATING, AND ADAPTING TO GPS

a. The low-strength data transmission signals from GPS satellites are vulnerable to various
anomalies that can significantly reduce the reliability of the navigation signal. The GPS signal
is vulnerable and has many uses in aviation (e.g., communication, navigation, surveillance,
safety systems and automation); therefore, pilots must place additional emphasis on closely
monitoring aircraft equipment performance for any anomalies and promptly inform Air Traffic
Control (ATC) of any apparent GPS degradation. Pilots should also be prepared to operate
without GPS navigation systems.
b. GPS signals are vulnerable to intentional and unintentional interference from a wide variety
of sources, including radars, microwave links, ionosphere effects, solar activity, multi-path
error, satellite communications, GPS repeaters, and even some systems onboard the air-
craft. In general, these types of unintentional interference are localized and intermittent. Of
greater and growing concern is the intentional and unauthorized interference of GPS signals

c. Manufacturers, operators, and air traffic controllers should be aware of the general impacts
of GPS jamming and/or spoofing, which include, but are not limited to:

2. Inability to use hybrid GPS inertial systems for navigation.
3. Loss of, or degraded, performance-based navigation (PBN) capability (e.g., inability to

4. Unreliable triggering of Terrain Awareness and Warning Systems (TAWS).
5. Inaccurate aircraft position on navigation display (e.g., moving map and electronic flight
bag).
6. Loss of, or erroneous, Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) outputs.
7. Unexpected effects when navigating with conventional NAVAIDS (e.g., if the aircraft is
spoofed from the intended flight path, autotuning will not select the nearby NAVAID).
8. Unanticipated position-dependent flight management system effects (e.g., erroneous
insufficient fuel indication).

example, could help detect a compromised GPS signal. Pilots transitioning to VOR naviga-
tion in response to GPS anomalies should refer to the Chart Supplement U.S. to identify air-
ports with available conventional approaches associated with the VOR Minimum Operational
Network (MON) program. (Reference 1-1-3f.)
e. Prior to departure, the FAA recommends operators to:
1. Be aware of potential risk locations.
2. Check for any relevant Notices to Airmen (NOTAMs).
3. Plan fuel contingencies.

paragraphs: 이 블록은 이번 Section 2 패치에서 임의 요약으로 빠지는 내용을 막기 위해 해당 페이지의 원문 텍스트 레이어를 그대로 보존한 검수용 원문이다.
4. Plan to use conventional NAVAIDs and appropriate arrival/approach procedures at the
destination.
5. Follow the detailed guidance from the respective Original Equipment Manufacturer
(OEM).
f. During flight, the FAA recommends operators do the following:
1. Be vigilant for any indication that the aircraft’s GPS is disrupted by reviewing the manu-
facturer’s guidance for that specific aircraft type and avionics equipage. Verify the air-
craft position by means of conventional NAVAIDs, when available. Indications of jam-
ming and/or spoofing may include:
(a) Changes in actual navigation performance.
(b) Aircraft clock changes (e.g., incorrect time).
(c) Incorrect Flight Management System (FMS) position.
(d) Large shift in displayed GPS position.
(e) Primary Flight Display (PFD)/Navigation Display (ND) warnings about position
error.
(f) Other aircraft reporting clock issues, position errors, or requesting vectors.
2. Assess operational risks and limitations linked to the loss of GPS capability, including
any on-board systems requiring inputs from a GPS signal.
3. Ensure NAVAIDs critical to the operation for the intended route/approach are available.
4. Remain prepared to revert to conventional instrument flight procedures.
5. Promptly notify ATC if they experience GPS anomalies. Pilots should not inform ATC of
GPS jamming and/or spoofing when flying through known NOTAMed testing areas
unless they require ATC assistance. (See paragraph 1-1-13)
g. Post flight, the FAA recommends operators to:
1. Document any GPS jamming and/or spoofing in the maintenance log to ensure all faults
are cleared.
2. File a detailed report at the reporting site: Report a GPS Anomaly Federal Aviation
Administration, www.faa.gov/air_traffic/nas/gps_reports.
